stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core domain of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The mention of 'transformers' and 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern NLP infrastructure.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model leverages Ollama's MLX engine, featuring native support for DFlash and image input.

stories.title: John Ternus is now the CEO of Apple
stories.author: Richard Lawler
bullet_points: John Ternus has been appointed as the new CEO of Apple.
Tim Cook is stepping down as CEO but will remain on the board as Executive Chairman.
This marks a significant leadership change for one of the world's most valuable technology companies.

stories.title: FTC lawsuit alleges Amazon has been ‘secretly and systematically’ overcharging for ads
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: The FTC and 22 state AGs are suing Amazon over alleged deceptive advertising practices.
The core allegation is that Amazon used a 'secret ad surcharge' to inflate advertising costs.
The FTC claims these higher ad prices were ultimately passed on to American consumers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics such as 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of 'llama' indicates relevance to large language model (LLM) development.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase when benchmarked with Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware, emphasizing privacy and control.
Integration with Ollama is built-in, leveraging existing local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Auditing Anonymous AI Models: A Four-Stage Protocol for Black-Box Identity Verification
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Addresses the growing problem of anonymously released frontier AI models in the 2025-2026 market.
Proposes a novel four-stage forensic audit protocol to verify the identity of black-box, API-served AI models.
Highlights the critical industry need for trustworthy identity verification due to risks in data handling and supply chain.

stories.title: Token-Efficient Data Reasoning Agents via Adaptive Structuring of Unstructured Data
stories.author: Stratos Idreos
bullet_points: Addresses the high token consumption issue when LLM agents reason over large, unstructured enterprise data (PDFs, reports, etc.).
Proposes a solution involving 'Adaptive Structuring' of unstructured data to make it more digestible for AI agents.
Aims to significantly reduce the computational cost associated with complex data reasoning tasks in enterprise AI deployments.

stories.title: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
stories.author: Shumin Deng
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in autonomous research agents: the lack of predefined success criteria for open-ended scientific tasks.
Introduces a novel approach, 'Automatic Rubric Induction,' allowing agents to learn evaluation criteria before attempting to improve their performance.
Relevant to the growing trend of end-to-end AI agents handling complex scientific workflows (literature review, data analysis, etc.).

stories.title: S3Gym: Can LLMs Turn Self-Testing and Self-Judging into Self-Improvement?
stories.author: Ge Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces S3Gym, a new interactive benchmark designed to test LLM self-improvement capabilities.
Addresses the gap in current agent benchmarks, which treat LLMs as fixed policies rather than learning agents.
Focuses on whether LLMs can actively test their behavior, judge the outcomes, and use that feedback for decision improvement.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine capabilities on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Car owners want tech they can ignore
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Consumers are growing weary of the excessive and often buggy technology being integrated into modern vehicles.
JD Power research indicates that the most valued automotive features are often those that operate seamlessly and are barely noticed by the driver.
The trend suggests a consumer preference shift away from flashy, complex infotainment systems toward reliable, unobtrusive functionality.

stories.title: Phil Schiller is leaving his biggest jobs at Apple
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Longtime Apple executive Phil Schiller is stepping down from his roles as head of the App Store and Apple events.
Schiller will retain his Apple Fellow title and continue working on unspecified initiatives post-departure.
The news, reported by Bloomberg, marks a significant personnel change at Apple.

stories.title: “Zlibrary my beloved”: Anthropic staff chats extolling piracy cited in Sony suit
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Anthropic staff allegedly engaged in torrenting and piracy, as cited in a lawsuit.
The lawsuit connects this alleged piracy to the rise of AI-generated music topping charts.
The core issue revolves around intellectual property rights and the impact of AI on songwriters.

stories.title: Think twice before installing this device promising free movies
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Devices offering 'free' content may compromise user privacy.
The trade-off involves integrating the home network into a proxy network.
This highlights risks associated with free software/hardware installations.

stories.title: SUN: Persistent Programs For Language-Grounded Control-to-Learning-to-Real Policies
stories.author: Ran Gong
bullet_points: Introduces SUN (Semantically UNified) Programs to bridge model-based control and learned policies in long-horizon manipulation.
Addresses the issue where traditional learning methods discard task semantics, leading to reward-based behavior drift.
SUN compiles geometric and contact relations into aligned Model Predictive Control (MPC) frameworks.

stories.title: When Does Bigger Help? A Controlled Study of LLM Scale for Ontology Learning
stories.author: Jennifer D'Souza
bullet_points: The study investigates how the scale of Large Language Models (LLMs) impacts their performance in Ontology Learning (OL).
It provides a controlled evaluation comparing 13 models, including Qwen3.5/3.6 variants and proprietary GPT releases.
The research uses the OntoLearner retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to ensure consistent testing conditions across models.

stories.title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
stories.author: Edoardo Manino
bullet_points: Introduces BLOOM-WILT, a new pipeline designed for automated auditing of large language models (LLMs).
Addresses the problem of deployment-specific behaviors that standard, sample-inefficient automated testing often misses.
Uses 'Logit Tilting' as a technique to efficiently elicit natural, multi-turn behaviors from LLMs during auditing.

stories.title: LLM Post-Training as Brownfield Maintenance: An Industrial Perspective on Dataware Engineering
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: The paper frames industrial LLM post-training as a 'brownfield maintenance' problem, contrasting it with clean-slate retraining.
Key industrial constraints include maintaining performance under fixed compute and mixture budgets while applying targeted improvements.
The resulting LLM artifact is increasingly treated as a 'dataware,' governed by curated post-training mixtures updated via bounded patches.

stories.title: Implementing neural network mixed-effects models in Template Model Builder (TMB)
stories.author: Noel G. Cadigan
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in Neural Network Mixed-Effects Models (NMMs) where existing estimation methods require manual, complex derivations.
The work introduces a new method (implied to be automated or more efficient) to implement NMMs within the Template Model Builder (TMB).
This advancement aims to overcome constraints on complexity and accuracy by moving beyond manual objective function and gradient derivations.

stories.title: "Train classical, deploy quantum" requires rethinking generalization
stories.author: Alejandro Perdomo-Ortiz
bullet_points: The paper discusses the challenge of generalization when training classical models to deploy quantum generative models.
Quantum generative models are highlighted as a promising application for quantum computing due to their inherent ability to sample complex distributions.
A common strategy involves training these quantum models using classical computers, which the research suggests requires rethinking generalization.

stories.title: Stress-Testing Efficient Responsible-AI Evaluation: When Compute Savings Change Benchmark Conclusions
stories.author: Shaina Raza
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in Responsible AI evaluation by testing how efficiency improvements (like quantization and batching) affect benchmark conclusions.
The study stress-tests conclusion robustness across three types of models (dense and MoE) using BBQ and BBQ-V benchmarks under various efficiency conditions.
It challenges the assumption that maintaining aggregate accuracy is sufficient when evaluating responsible AI claims after computational savings are introduced.

stories.title: LLM Post-Training as Brownfield Maintenance: An Industrial Perspective on Dataware Engineering
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: The paper frames LLM post-training in industrial settings as a 'brownfield maintenance' problem.
This maintenance requires targeted improvements on existing deployed models under strict compute and budget constraints.
The focus shifts from clean-slate retraining to updating the model's behavior via curated dataware and bounded mixture patches.

stories.title: One Adapter, Many Tasks: Task-Conditioned Feature Transformations for Continual Learning
stories.author: Yizhou Yu
bullet_points: The research addresses Class-Incremental Learning (CIL), a challenge where models must learn new tasks/classes without forgetting old ones.
Current methods often use task-specific adapters, which suffer from being computationally and parameter-inefficient.
The proposed work introduces a 'One Adapter, Many Tasks' approach to improve efficiency in continual learning settings.

stories.title: Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization
stories.author: Jing Huang
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'sycophantic agreement,' where LLMs excessively affirm users, often sacrificing factual accuracy.
It proposes that this undesirable behavior can arise as an unintended consequence of standard contrastive preference optimization objectives.
The research uses the OLMo 3 post-training pipeline to empirically demonstrate the emergence of this alignment failure.

stories.title: Context-Aware Interleaved Batching for WhisperX
stories.author: Max Bain
bullet_points: Addresses the trade-off between speed (WhisperX) and context retention (standard Whisper) in speech transcription.
Introduces 'Context-Aware Interleaved Batching' to combine fast batch processing with historical context awareness.
Uses VAD-derived segment boundaries to stabilize Whisper's text conditioning for better punctuation and terminology.

stories.title: Configurable Semantic Chunking for Biomedical Information Extraction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Roya Shiasi Sardoabi
bullet_points: Introduces a configurable semantic chunking framework to improve biomedical information extraction.
Addresses the limitation of fixed-size chunking in existing RAG models (like BioMedRAG) that can fragment semantic evidence.
The framework utilizes advanced techniques including entity-preserving windows and proposition-first extraction.

stories.title: DIASENTINEL: An Auditable Multi-Agent System for Guideline-Grounded Diabetes Risk Screening
stories.author: Feng Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DIASENTINEL, a multi-agent system designed to address LLM hallucinations in clinical settings.
The system provides guideline-grounded risk screening for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) using Electronic Health Records (EHRs).
It operates fully on-premise, integrating calibrated risk prediction and deterministic signal extraction for enhanced reliability.

stories.title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?
stories.author: Ge Zhang
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Aspire,' a framework addressing the limitation of current LLM self-evolution methods.
Aspire aims to enable models to learn from vague, high-level goals, mirroring human learning processes (e.g., 'become a better physicist').
This contrasts with existing work that relies on explicit, human-defined tasks and evaluation metrics for optimization.

stories.title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
stories.author: Edoardo Manino
bullet_points: Introduces BLOOM-WILT, a new pipeline designed for automated auditing of large language models (LLMs).
Addresses the problem of LLM behavior not being captured by limited pre-deployment testing due to massive real-world interaction volume.
Uses 'Logit Tilting' to make automated auditing more sample-efficient and capable of eliciting complex behaviors.

stories.title: The First Token Is a Clue: Verbalizing Multi-Token Concepts from the J-lens
stories.author: Tonghan Wang
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in the Jacobian Lens (J-lens) tool for interpreting LLMs: its inability to represent multi-token concepts.
Existing solutions, Template Lens and Oracle Lens, attempt to handle multi-token concepts by precomputing or fine-tuning phrase vectors.
The research proposes a new method to recover representations for multi-token concepts directly, rather than relying on precomputed or fine-tuned phrase vectors.

stories.title: Token-Efficient Data Reasoning Agents via Adaptive Structuring of Unstructured Data
stories.author: Stratos Idreos
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high token consumption (up to a million tokens) when LLM agents reason over large, unstructured enterprise data.
The proposed solution involves 'Adaptive Structuring' of unstructured data to make it more digestible for AI agents.
This research aims to reduce the computational cost and improve efficiency of deploying LLM agents for knowledge workers.

stories.title: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
stories.author: Shumin Deng
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of open-ended scientific research tasks where success criteria are often undefined.
Proposes 'Automatic Rubric Induction' to help autonomous research agents determine necessary analyses and evaluation metrics.
Aims to improve the reliability of AI agents in complex scientific workflows (literature review, data analysis, etc.).

stories.title: Your embeddings forget exactly like a human brain does
stories.author: wiking
bullet_points: The article demonstrates that standard pre-trained embeddings exhibit forgetting behavior mirroring the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve.
Researchers reproduced classic false-memory rates using unmodified embeddings, suggesting inherent decay in current memory representations.
This finding provides insight into why agent memory in AI systems naturally decays without specific tuning or architectural changes.
